proposal.summary: PubMed record pages are served to automated clients as an HTTP 203 JavaScript challenge interstitial whose challengeId is regenerated per request, so the body is never byte-stable and carries no article content to hash.
proposal.sopBasis: docs/citation-verification-sop.md, 'Content digests and tiered staleness': dynamic pages whose body changes per fetch must not receive a digest; omit it rather than record a value that will false-positive.

assessment.method: Three sequential GETs per sample URL, 2s apart, redirect-followed, response bodies hashed with SHA-256 and compared. Repeated under the audit probe User-Agent, a desktop browser User-Agent and no User-Agent header; all three client shapes received the identical 5590-byte 203 interstitial.
assessment.notes: The interstitial's <title> is the bare hostname 'pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov', not the article title, and no abstract markup is present. HTTP 203 is by definition non-authoritative (RFC 9110: the payload was modified from the origin server's 200 response by a transforming proxy), so this body is not the source a verifier read. Corroborated independently by docs/liver-cancer-sarcopenia-citation-verification-2026-disposition.md, which records that PubMed HTML was bot-walled on 2026-10-03 and that metadata and abstracts were read through NCBI E-utilities instead.

digestibleAlternative.notes: NCBI E-utilities efetch returns the authoritative PubMed record for the same PMID as byte-stable XML containing ArticleTitle, Abstract, PMID, DOI and publication status, so a retraction or correction changes it. This is the anchor a qualified human should digest at the next verification of a PubMed source. It is recorded here as an available path only: no digest has been backfilled onto any existing reference, because a digest computed after the fact is not anchored to its recorded sourceCheckedOn date and the SOP forbids it.

review.note: The volatility measurement is reproducible and objective. The qualified-human sign-off recorded here is for accepting the exemption as standing digest policy for this source class, and for deciding whether future PubMed verifications digest the E-utilities anchor instead.

proposal.summary: eCFR /current/ HTML embeds a per-response Content-Security-Policy nonce on its analytics script tag, so the body differs on most fetches even though the regulatory text is unchanged.
proposal.sopBasis: docs/citation-verification-sop.md, 'Content digests and tiered staleness': dynamic pages whose body changes per fetch must not receive a digest; omit it rather than record a value that will false-positive.

assessment.method: Five sequential GETs, 6s apart, redirect-followed, bodies hashed with SHA-256 and compared; the first differing character region was then located to identify the varying token.
assessment.notes: Byte length is constant and only the CSP nonce varies, which makes this easy to mistake for a stable body: an earlier three-fetch sample returned one repeated digest while the five-fetch sample returned four distinct digests. A digest recorded here would false-positive on nonce rotation rather than on any change to the regulation, which is exactly the failure the SOP's omission rule exists to prevent. Where drift detection is wanted for a CFR section, digest a pinned annual-edition or XML rendering rather than /current/ HTML. Covers one verified reference (38 CFR 3.310, ocd.json).

review.note: Narrow: /current/ HTML only. Annual-edition and XML renderings are not covered and remain digestible.

proposal.summary: Oxford Academic serves automated clients an HTTP 403 bot-wall interstitial with a per-request varying body, so neither the article content nor a stable digest is obtainable by probe.
proposal.sopBasis: docs/citation-verification-sop.md, 'Content digests and tiered staleness': dynamic pages whose body changes per fetch must not receive a digest; omit it rather than record a value that will false-positive.

assessment.method: Three sequential GETs, 2s apart, redirect-followed, bodies hashed with SHA-256 and compared.
assessment.observedVaryingToken: 403 bot-wall interstitial body carrying a per-request varying token
assessment.notes: HTTP 403 is already classified bot-blocked by the decay probe's BODY_FETCH_FALLBACK_STATUSES path, so this entry does not change link-rot accounting; it records that no digest can be captured for this source class by automated means. Covers one verified reference (hyperaldosteronism.json).

review.note: A qualified human reading this article in a browser may be able to capture a digest of the rendered article HTML; that decision is theirs and is not recorded here.

cornellReferences.rationale: Chronic pain and depression frequently co-occur and can be associated with reduced physical, mental, and social functioning. This population-level relationship does not by itself establish an individual medical nexus.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The published knowledge base includes this relationship as an association: Abdominal hernia → documented chronic pain or functional limitation, if present → claimed causation or worsening of depressive disorder.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR § 3.310 is established by the current evidence; the guard explicitly limits the claim to association.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Abdominal hernia → documented chronic pain or functional limitation, if present → claimed causation or worsening of depressive disorder.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. Abdominal hernia → documented chronic pain or functional limitation, if present → claimed causation or worsening of depressive disorder. It is not asserted that the primary caused or aggravated the secondary in any individual.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Mental health evaluation and diagnosis; Documentation of chronic pain, functional limitations, and their timing; Clinical opinion addressing the individual relationship when a secondary theory is asserted
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Other causes not yet identified in this mapping

reference.note: Legal framework for secondary service connection; does not establish the underlying medical relationship.

cornellReferences.rationale: When NSAID treatment for rheumatoid-arthritis pain is documented in the individual record, observational evidence associating NSAID use with GERD symptoms supports a bounded medication-related research pathway. The clinical source does not establish that rheumatoid arthritis itself causes GERD or that an NSAID caused or aggravated an individual veteran's GERD; the actual prescription indication, exposure, chronology, diagnosis, and competing gastrointestinal contributors remain essential.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Rheumatoid arthritis → individually documented NSAID treatment for RA pain, if present → claimed contribution to or worsening of clinically characterized GERD; the treatment-exposure link must come from the individual medical record. Observational evidence associating NSAID use with GERD symptoms supports this bounded medication-related research pathway.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: The guard explicitly declines to establish individual causation or aggravation under 38 CFR § 3.310: the clinical source does not establish that rheumatoid arthritis itself causes GERD or that an NSAID caused or aggravated an individual veteran's GERD. Chronology, prescription indication and exposure, and competing gastrointestinal contributors require case-specific medical assessment.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Rheumatoid arthritis → individually documented NSAID treatment for RA pain, if present → claimed contribution to or worsening of clinically characterized GERD; the treatment-exposure link must come from the individual medical record and the medication-to-GERD link still requires case-specific medical assessment.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. NSAID treatment for rheumatoid-arthritis pain, when individually documented, is associated with GERD symptoms, but the current evidence does not establish that the medication caused or aggravated an individual veteran's GERD. The medication-to-GERD link still requires case-specific medical assessment, and no nexus probability is asserted.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Prescription history identifying the specific NSAID exposure, RA indication, dose, duration, and timing; Documented GERD diagnosis and clinical characterization; Evaluation of alternative GERD causes and risk factors; Qualified medical opinion addressing the individual medication-related relationship when asserted
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Other causes not yet identified in this mapping
